```{r read data, include=FALSE}
data <- read.csv("data/main_data.csv")

# slice top 2 rows of redundant info

data <- data %>%
  slice(-(1:2))

# apply exclusion criteria (exclude pps who complete in under half the median time)

data$Duration..in.seconds. <- as.numeric(data$Duration..in.seconds.)

cutoff <- median(data$Duration..in.seconds., na.rm = TRUE) / 2

# median is 635.5 seconds, half is 317.75 = 27 exclusions (2.7% of sample)

data <- data %>%
  filter(Duration..in.seconds. > cutoff)

#add row number identifier

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(id = row_number()) %>%
  dplyr::select(id, everything())
```

```{r create functions, include=FALSE}

# converting classic likert scale to numeric 

likert_numeric <- function(response) {
  
  # Trim leading and trailing whitespace and convert to lowercase
  response_cleaned <- tolower(trimws(response))
  
  # Define the mapping with all lowercase keys
  mapping <- c(
    "strongly disagree" = 1,
    "disagree" = 2,
    "somewhat disagree" = 3,
    "neither agree nor disagree" = 4,
    "somewhat agree" = 5,
    "agree" = 6,
    "strongly agree" = 7
  )
  
  # Return the mapped value, or NA if the response does not match
  return(ifelse(!is.na(mapping[response_cleaned]), mapping[response_cleaned], NA))
  
  # convert to numeric
  return(as.numeric(numeric_values))
}

# convert to 0, 1 factor

make_factor <- function(data, cols) {
  data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(across(
      dplyr::all_of(cols),
      ~ factor(.x, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("0","1"))
    ))
}

# set factor levels for ideology variables

level_ideology <- function(data, vars) {
  ideology_levels <- c(
    "Strongly left-leaning",
    "Left-leaning",
    "Somewhat left-leaning",
    "Neither left nor right leaning",
    "Somewhat right-leaning",
    "Right-leaning",
    "Strongly right-leaning"
  )
  
  data %>%
    mutate(across(
      all_of(vars),
      ~ factor(.x, levels = ideology_levels, ordered = TRUE)
    ))
}

# set factor levels for individual categorical variables

# Convert multiple character vars to factors with specified level orders
# - levels_map: named list with all pre-specific vectors
# - ordered_cols: character vector of column names that should be ordered factors
# - append_unknown: if TRUE, unseen values in the data are appended to the end of levels
# - warn_unknown: if TRUE, warn about unseen values
set_factor_levels <- function(data, levels_map, ordered_cols = character(),
                              append_unknown = TRUE, warn_unknown = TRUE) {

  stopifnot(is.list(levels_map), !is.null(names(levels_map)))
  cols <- intersect(names(levels_map), names(data))
  if (length(cols) == 0) return(data)

  data %>%
    mutate(across(all_of(cols), ~ {
      lvls <- levels_map[[cur_column()]]
      x <- .x

      # Handle values not in the provided levels
      if (append_unknown) {
        miss <- setdiff(unique(x), lvls)
        if (warn_unknown && length(miss) > 0) {
          warning(sprintf(
            "Column '%s': appending %d unknown level(s): %s",
            cur_column(), length(miss), paste(miss, collapse = ", ")
          ))
        }
        lvls <- c(lvls, setdiff(miss, lvls))
      } else {
        miss <- setdiff(unique(x), lvls)
        if (warn_unknown && length(miss) > 0) {
          warning(sprintf(
            "Column '%s': %d value(s) not in provided levels will become NA: %s",
            cur_column(), length(miss), paste(miss, collapse = ", ")
          ))
        }
      }

      factor(x, levels = lvls, ordered = cur_column() %in% ordered_cols)
    }))
}

# Mean-score items

mean_score <- function(data, vars, new_name) {
  data %>%
    mutate(
      !!new_name := rowMeans(across(all_of(vars)), na.rm = TRUE)
    )
}

```

#### What was the demographic breakdown of the sample?

```{r table, include=FALSE}

# function to create demographic breakdown table
demographic_table <- function(data, vars, total_n) {
  bind_rows(lapply(vars, function(v) {
    data %>%
      count(!!sym(v), name = "N") %>%
      mutate(
        Variable = v,
        Level = as.character(!!sym(v)),
        Percent = round(100 * N / total_n, 1)
      ) %>%
      dplyr::select(Variable, Level, N, Percent)
  })) %>%
    arrange(match(Variable, vars)) %>%
    mutate(
      Percent = paste0(Percent, "%")
    )
}

# specify variables in the order you want them
vars <- c("region", "gender", "education", "ethnicity", "self_ideology", "interest")

# create table
sample_table <- demographic_table(sample, vars, total_n = 985)

# pretty print
kable(sample_table, align = c("l","l","r","r"),
      col.names = c("Variable", "Category", "N", "%"))
```

#### How did the participants perceive the ideology of the political parties? Was this fairly uniform? How did it compare relative to the ideology of the self (collected pre-manipulation)?

```{r include=FALSE}

ideology_levels <- c(
  "Strongly left-leaning",
  "Left-leaning",
  "Somewhat left-leaning",
  "Neither left nor right leaning",
  "Somewhat right-leaning",
  "Right-leaning",
  "Strongly right-leaning"
)

sample <- sample %>%
  mutate(
    alliance_ideology = factor(alliance_ideology, levels = ideology_levels, ordered = TRUE),
    sdp_ideology      = factor(sdp_ideology,      levels = ideology_levels, ordered = TRUE)
  )

```


Below shows how the political ideology of both parties were rated by participants. The most common response option for both was 'neither left nor right leaning'.

```{r echo=FALSE}

df_counts <- sample %>%
  mutate(
    alliance_ideology = factor(alliance_ideology, levels = ideology_levels, ordered = TRUE),
    sdp_ideology      = factor(sdp_ideology,      levels = ideology_levels, ordered = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(alliance_ideology, sdp_ideology) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Category"
  ) %>%
  count(Variable, Category, name = "N") %>%
  tidyr::complete(Variable, Category, fill = list(N = 0))

# create %

df_pct <- df_counts %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Variable) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pct = N / sum(N)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# Name 

var_labels <- c(
  alliance_ideology = "Perceived Alliance ideology",
  sdp_ideology      = "Perceived SDP ideology"
)

# colours

var_colors <- c(
  alliance_ideology = "#C49A00",  # yellow
  sdp_ideology      = "#800000"   # red
)

# plot

ggplot(df_pct, aes(x = Category, y = pct, fill = Variable)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 0.1)), hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, labeller = as_labeller(var_labels), ncol = 1) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.15))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = var_colors, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% of respondents") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

```

However, perceptions differed between parties (comparison of ordinal distributions: Stuart–Maxwell X2(6)=115.2, p<.001). A paired Wilcoxon test indicated SDP was perceived as more right-wing than Alliance (Hodges–Lehmann shift = +0.5 categories, 95% CI [0.50, 0.50], p < .001). Among non-tied pairs, 60.2% placed SDP to the right of Alliance (p < .001).

```{r alliance sdp distrubutions, include=FALSE}

# Square contingency table of paired ratings (Alliance rows, SDP cols)
tab_party <- table(sample$alliance_ideology, sample$sdp_ideology)

# Stuart–Maxwell and Bhapkar tests of marginal homogeneity
library(DescTools)
StuartMaxwellTest(tab_party)
BhapkarTest(tab_party)

# check in which direction

a  <- as.integer(sample$alliance_ideology)
s  <- as.integer(sample$sdp_ideology)
ok <- complete.cases(a, s)
d  <- s[ok] - a[ok]   # positive => SDP rated more right-wing

# Descriptives of the paired shift
table_diff <- table(d)
prop.table(table_diff)        # proportions of each shift value
median(d); mean(d)            # median/mean shift in categories
mean(d > 0); mean(d < 0); mean(d == 0)

# Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank (Hodges–Lehmann shift + CI)
w_two_sided <- wilcox.test(s[ok], a[ok], paired = TRUE, exact = FALSE, conf.int = TRUE)
w_greater   <- wilcox.test(s[ok], a[ok], paired = TRUE, exact = FALSE,
                           conf.int = TRUE, alternative = "greater")  # tests "SDP > Alliance"
w_two_sided
w_two_sided$estimate  # HL location shift (in category units)
w_two_sided$conf.int  # CI for the shift

# Sign test (robust, ignores magnitudes)
npos <- sum(d > 0); nneg <- sum(d < 0)
binom.test(npos, npos + nneg, p = 0.5, alternative = "greater")

```

Furthermore, chi-squared tests indicated that there is a correlation between self-identified ideology and the ideology each party was perceived to have. Due to small N in some of the categories in the 7x7 grid, Monte Carlo simulations are used to estimate p-values. A positive and significant association was found for both parties, indicating that participants tended to interpret the ideology of the party in line with their own. For Alliance, the test indicated clear dependence between variables, X2 = 156.56, P <.001.For SDP, the result was similarly significant, x2 = 124.87, p<.001.These results reject independence for both parties, indicating that respondents’ self-placements on the left–right scale are systematically related to how left- or right-wing they perceive the parties to be.

```{r include=FALSE}

# Self vs ALLIANCE
alliance_association <- table(sample$self_ideology, sample$alliance_ideology)

# Use Monte Carlo p-value (robust when some expected < 5)
chisq_a_mc <- chisq.test(alliance_association, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 50000)
chisq_a_mc

# Self vs SDP
sdp_association <- table(sample$self_ideology, sample$sdp_ideology)

# Use Monte Carlo p-value (robust when some expected < 5)
chisq_s_mc <- chisq.test(sdp_association, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 50000)
chisq_s_mc

```

```{r wide to long, include=FALSE}

# repeated measures final column names

r_measures <- c(
  "skill","princ","emp","know","sinc","kind","comp","truth","warm",
  "agree1","agree2","proact","look","intent","open","use","compliant",
  "policy","ideology","support","familiar"
)

# 1) Make the two-row-per-id trial table 
trial_long <- main %>%
  dplyr::select(id, vote, self_ideology, matches("^trial(1|2)_(party|motive|imprint|label)$")) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^trial(1|2)_(party|motive|imprint|label)$"),
    names_to = c("trial", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "^trial(1|2)_(.*)$"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    trial = as.integer(trial),
    party = as.integer(party),
    motive = as.integer(motive),
    imprint = as.integer(imprint)
  )

# 2) Prepare party-specific data for alliance (a_/alliance_) and sdp (s_/sdp_)

# Make alliance-by-id by stripping prefixes and adding _A suffix
alliance_by_id <- data %>%
  dplyr::select(id, starts_with("a_"), starts_with("alliance_")) %>%
  rename_with(~ sub("^a_", "", .x),           starts_with("a_")) %>%
  rename_with(~ sub("^alliance_", "", .x),    starts_with("alliance_")) %>%
  rename_with(~ ifelse(.x == "id", .x, paste0(.x, "_A")))

# Make sdp-by-id with _S suffix
sdp_by_id <- data %>%
  dplyr::select(id, starts_with("s_"), starts_with("sdp_")) %>%
  rename_with(~ sub("^s_",   "", .x), starts_with("s_")) %>%
  rename_with(~ sub("^sdp_", "", .x), starts_with("sdp_")) %>%
  rename_with(~ ifelse(.x == "id", .x, paste0(.x, "_S")))

# 4) Join both party blocks onto the trial table
long_data <- trial_long %>%
  left_join(alliance_by_id, by = "id") %>%
  left_join(sdp_by_id,      by = "id") %>%
  mutate(
    !!!set_names(
      lapply(r_measures, function(m) {
        a <- sym(paste0(m, "_A"))
        s <- sym(paste0(m, "_S"))
        # build an expression that will be evaluated in the data mask
        expr(if_else(.data$party == 0L, !!a, !!s))
      }),
      r_measures
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(id, trial, party, motive, imprint, label, all_of(r_measures), vote, self_ideology) %>%
  arrange(id, trial)


```

### Checking randomisation

#### Was political ideology, pre-existing knowledge of party, and pre-existing party support successfully randomised into conditions?

```{r randomised ideology, echo=FALSE}

# create new column retaining only the two experimental conditions

long_data <- long_data %>%
  mutate(
    cond = case_match(label,
                      c("A_F_C", "S_F_C") ~ 1,
                      c("A_F_D", "S_F_D") ~ 2,
                      c("A_W_C", "S_W_C") ~ 3,
                      c("A_W_D", "S_W_D") ~ 4
    )
  )

# set factor levels

long_data <- long_data %>%
  mutate(cond = factor(cond, levels = 1:4,
                       labels = c("Cond 1","Cond 2","Cond 3","Cond 4")))

# numeric

long_data$support_r <- as.numeric(long_data$support)

# checking numerical covariates with an omnibus f-test

anova(lm(policy ~ cond, data = long_data))

anova(lm(self_ideology ~ cond, data = long_data))

anova(lm(support ~ cond, data = long_data))

# checking pre-existing knowledge (familiar)

familiar_randomisation <- table(long_data$familiar, long_data$cond)

chisq_fam <- chisq.test(familiar_randomisation, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 50000)
chisq_fam

# checking pre-existing support

summary(lm(support ~ cond, data = long_data))

```

### Descriptive variable distributions

```{r, echo=FALSE}

outcomes <- c("skill","princ","emp","know","sinc","comp","kind","warm","truth")

# sample skewness and excess kurtosis (standardised moments)
.skew <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  n <- length(x); if (n < 3) return(NA_real_)
  m <- mean(x); s <- sd(x); if (s == 0) return(0)
  mean(((x - m)/s)^3)
}
.kurt_excess <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  n <- length(x); if (n < 4) return(NA_real_)
  m <- mean(x); s <- sd(x); if (s == 0) return(0)
  mean(((x - m)/s)^4) - 3
}

# ---- Overall distribution table with skew & kurtosis ----
dist_tbl <- long_data %>%
  summarise(across(
    all_of(outcomes),
    list(
      N        = ~ sum(!is.na(.x)),
      Mean     = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      SD       = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Skewness = ~ .skew(.x),
      Kurtosis = ~ .kurt_excess(.x),
      Median   = ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      P25      = ~ quantile(.x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
      P75      = ~ quantile(.x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
      Min      = ~ min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      Max      = ~ max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .names = "{.col}__{.fn}"
  )) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = c("Variable", ".value"),
               names_sep = "__") %>%
  arrange(Variable)

# print
dist_tbl %>%
  mutate(Variable = str_to_title(Variable)) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(
    Variable = "Outcome",
    N = "N",
    Mean = "Mean", SD = "SD",
    Skewness = "Skewness", Kurtosis = "Kurtosis (excess)",
    Median = "Median",
    P25 = "25th pct", P75 = "75th pct",
    Min = "Min", Max = "Max"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(Mean, SD, Skewness, Kurtosis, Median, P25, P75, Min, Max),
             decimals = 2) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Outcome Distributions (overall)")

dist_tbl

# by condition

dist_by_cond <- long_data %>%
  group_by(cond) %>%
  summarise(across(
    all_of(outcomes),
    list(
      N = ~ sum(!is.na(.x)),
      Mean = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      SD = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .names = "{.col}__{.fn}"
  ), .groups = "drop") %>%
```

### Scale reliability

```{r}

# Trustworthiness (all 9 items)
trust_items <- long_data[, c("skill","princ","emp","know","sinc","comp","kind","warm","truth")]

# Competence
```

### Manipulation checks

It was intended that the intentionality (motive) condition increased the perception that the political party shared information openly, while keeping perceptions of legal compliance and information availability constant. This was partially supported. The motive condition indeed increased perceptions that the political party shared information openly (see tables below), and they were not perceived as being more legally compliant. However, perceptions that the information was available for the public to view were positively impacted by motive.

It was intended that the disclosure condition would not affect the perception that the advertisements were well-designed. This was not supported; the presence of a disclosure increased the perceived professionalism of a post. This effect was statistically significant. The effect of motive (which had nothing to do with the post design) was also positive, suggesting that this measure was confounded by perceptions of trustworthiness, e.g., the more the party was trusted, the more professional their advertisement was rated. Ultimately, this means this alternative theoretical explanation (that a disclosure increases trust through increasing how 'polished' a post looks) could not be ruled out.

*Log odds interpretation:*

*- probability = chance of 'yes' in each condition,*

*- log odds: how many 'yes' for every 'no' in each condition; *

*- odds ratio (multiplicative): comparison of odds across conditions e.g., the increase in odds for 'yes' vs 'no' in condition = 1 compared to condition = 0.*

```{r manipulation summaries, echo=FALSE}
# Labels for terms
coef_map <- c(
  "(Intercept)"      = "Intercept",
  "motive1"          = "Motive (ref = forced)",
  "imprint1"         = "Imprint = (ref = control text)",
  "party1"           = "Party (ref = Alliance)"
)


model_table <- function(model, title = deparse(substitute(model)),
                        include_intercept = FALSE, ci_level = 0.95,
                        digits = 2, p_digits = 3) {

  is_glm_binom <- inherits(model, "glm") && family(model)$family == "binomial"

  td <- tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = ci_level,
             exponentiate = is_glm_binom) %>%
    mutate(term = recode(term, !!!coef_map)) %>%
    { if (!include_intercept) filter(., term != "Intercept") else . } %>%
    transmute(
      Term       = term,
      Est        = estimate,
      SE         = std.error,
      `Lower CI` = conf.low,
      `Upper CI` = conf.high,
      p          = p.value
    )

  gt(td) %>%
    tab_header(title = title) %>%
    cols_label(
      Est = if (is_glm_binom) "OR" else "Estimate",
      SE = "SE"
    ) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = c(Est, SE, `Lower CI`, `Upper CI`), decimals = digits) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = p, decimals = p_digits)
}

print("motive condition manipulation check")

model_table(man_compliant_sim, "Compliant with regulatory law (check for motive)")
model_table(man_use_sim, "Information availability (check for motive)")

print("disclosure condition manipulation check")

model_table(man_look_sim,   "Well-designed advertisement (check for disclosure)")
```

```{r manipulation check effect sizes, include=FALSE}
# Helper: get p0 (motive=0) and p1 (motive=1)
get_probs <- function(fit) {
  pe <- as.data.frame(emmeans(fit, ~ motive, type = "response"))
  # ensure motive=0 first
  pe <- pe[order(pe$motive), ]
  list(p0 = pe$prob[1], p1 = pe$prob[2])
}
cohens_h <- function(p1, p0) 2*asin(sqrt(p1)) - 2*asin(sqrt(p0))
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
# TOST for the effect of imprint

cf  <- coef(summary(man_look_sim))["imprint1", ]
est <- unname(cf["Estimate"])
se  <- unname(cf["Std. Error"])
df  <- df.residual(man_look_sim)

sig <- sigma(man_look_sim)
est_d <- est / sig
se_d  <- se  / sig

delta_d <- 0.10  # SESOI in Cohen's d

# 90% CI for d
t95 <- qt(0.95, df)
ci90_d <- c(est_d - t95*se_d, est_d + t95*se_d)

# TOST p-value in d units (declare equivalence if p_TOST < .05)
t1 <- (est_d - (-delta_d)) / se_d
t2 <- (delta_d - est_d) / se_d
p1 <- pt(t1, df, lower.tail = FALSE)
p2 <- pt(t2, df, lower.tail = FALSE)
p_TOST <- max(p1, p2)

list(d = est_d, CI90_d = ci90_d, p_TOST = p_TOST,
     equivalent = (ci90_d[1] > -delta_d & ci90_d[2] < delta_d))
```

### Hypothesis testing

Below shows the pre-registered hypotheses, which specified a single hypothesis for every planned statistical test.H1 and H2 are the same three tests, and are included separately to demonstrate competing theoretical predictions. 

*"Due to competing theoretical claims, it is currently unclear which dimensions of trustworthiness will be impacted by different exposure levels of intentionality (see document 'theoretical_framing' for clarification of concepts).*

*Hypothesis 1, primary (benevolence and integrity impacted, but not competence)*

- H1a. Participants informed that a political party engages in intentional information disclosure will report higher perceptions of integrity compared to those informed a party only shares what is necessary.
- H1b: Participants informed that a political party engages in intentional information disclosure will report higher perceptions of benevolence compared to those informed a party only shares what is necessary.
- H1c: There will be no effect of intentionality on perceptions of competence.

*Hypothesis 2, alternative (competence impacted, but not benevolence and integrity)*

- H2a. Participants informed that a political party engages in intentional information disclosure will report higher perceptions of competence compared to those informed a party only shares what is necessary.
- H2b: There will be no effect of intentionality on perceptions of integrity.
- H2c: There will be no effect of intentionality on perceptions of benevolence.

*For hypotheses that predict no effect, these will be tested against a smallest effect size of interest (SESOI), which is outlined in the analysis plan. Statistical equivalence will be tested against this SESOI using a two one-sided test (TOST). If equivalence is supported, this will be interpreted as evidence for the null; if not, non-significant results will be treated as absence of evidence.*

*The hypotheses below will be tested. It is recognised they may be partially contingent on the outcomes of the above stated tests.*

*Hypothesis 3*

- H3a. Intentionality will moderate the effect of viewing an advertising disclosure on perceived trustworthiness, such that a disclosure will increase competence only when the political party is known to share information intentionally.
- H3b. Intentionality will moderate the effect of viewing an advertising disclosure on perceived trustworthiness, such that a disclosure will increase integrity only when the political party is known to share information intentionally.
- H3c. Intentionality will moderate the effect of viewing an advertising disclosure on perceived benevolence, such that a disclosure will increase benevolence only when the political party is known to share information intentionally.

*Hypothesis 4*

H4a. Intentionality will increase the likelihood of voting for a political party, and this effect will be mediated by perceptions of competence.
H4b. Intentionality will increase the likelihood of voting for a political party, and this effect will be mediated by perceptions of integrity.
H4c. Intentionality will increase the likelihood of voting for a political party, and this effect will be mediated by perceptions of benevolence."

### Testing H1-H3

Summary

Do interaction terms improve model fit?

Do model assumptions hold?

### Assumptions for MLE models

- Functional form (linearity), fitted vs residual
- Homogeneity of variance, scale location plot
- Normality of level-1 residuals, Q-Q plot
- Normality of random effects, Q-Q plot
- Level-2 leverage points 

```{r}

library(lme4)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# -------- helper to make a 3-panel diagnostic for an lmer model --------
diag_lmer <- function(fit, model_title = "Model", save_path = NULL) {
  # data for plots
  df <- data.frame(
    fitted  = fitted(fit),                          # conditional fitted values (incl. RE)
    sresid  = resid(fit, type = "pearson")          # Pearson residuals (≈ standardized)
  )
  df$resid <- resid(fit, type = "response")

  # A) Residuals vs Fitted (functional form)
  pA <- ggplot(df, aes(fitted, resid)) +
    geom_point(shape = 16, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
    labs(x = "Fitted values (conditional)", y = "Residuals",
         title = paste(model_title, "Linearity Check (Residuals vs Fitted)")) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11)

  # B) Scale–Location (homoscedasticity)
  pB <- ggplot(df, aes(fitted, sqrt(abs(sresid)))) +
    geom_point(shape = 16, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.4) +
    labs(x = "Fitted values (conditional)",
         y = expression(sqrt("|Pearson residuals|")),
         title = paste(model_title, "Level-1: Homoskedasticity Check (Scale–Location)")) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11)

  # C) Normal Q–Q (of Pearson residuals)
  qq <- qqnorm(df$sresid, plot.it = FALSE)
  qq_df <- data.frame(theoretical = qq$x, sample = qq$y)

  pC <- ggplot(qq_df, aes(theoretical, sample)) +
    geom_point(shape = 16, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = 2) +
    labs(x = "Theoretical Quantiles", y = "Sample Quantiles",
         title = paste(model_title, "Level-1: Normality Check (Normal Q–Q)")) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11)

  # combine vertically
  p <- (pA / pB / pC) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = paste(model_title, ": Inspecting Mixed-Model Assumptions"),
      subtitle = deparse(formula(fit)),
      tag_levels = "A"
    ) &
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))

  if (!is.null(save_path)) {
    ggsave(save_path, plot = p, width = 8.27, height = 11.69, units = "in", dpi = 300)
  }
  p
}

# ---- Example usage ----

diag_lmer(cov_b, model_title = "Model 3: benevolence", save_path = "assumption_plot/benevolence_lmer_diagnostics.png")

```

### Level-2 assumptions (residuals and leverage)

```{r l2 competence}

# Cook's D with influence.ME

infl_c <- influence(cov_c, group = "id")  # cluster-level influence object
cd   <- cooks.distance(infl_c)             # Cook’s D per cluster (id)
thr  <- 4/length(cd)                       # heuristic cutoff
sum(cd > thr) 

cd_df <- data.frame(
  id = 1:length(cd),
  cooksD = cd
)

comp_cook_l2 <- ggplot(cd_df, aes(x = id, y = cooksD)) +
  geom_col(fill = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = thr, color = "red3", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Cook's D by cluster",
    x = "Cluster index (id)",
    y = "Cook's distance (red line = 0.004)"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12)

# Q-Q plot of residuals

# Standardised random intercepts (z_b)
re <- ranef(cov_c, condVar = TRUE)$id
postVar <- attr(ranef(cov_c, condVar = TRUE)[[1]], "postVar")
z_b <- as.numeric(re[[1]] / sqrt(postVar[1, 1, ]))

# Q–Q plot
comp_qq_l2 <- ggplot(data.frame(z_b = z_b), aes(sample = z_b)) +
  stat_qq(shape = 16) +
  stat_qq_line(linetype = 2, alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(
    title = "Q–Q Plot of Standardised Level-2 Random Effects",
    x = "Theoretical Quantiles", y = "Sample Quantiles"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12)

# Combine the two plots vertically with patchwork
comp_l2_diagnostics <- (comp_qq_l2 / comp_cook_l2) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Level-2 Diagnostics for Competence Model",
    subtitle = "A: Normality of Random Effects   |   B: Cluster Influence (Cook’s D)",
    tag_levels = "A"   # labels them A, B automatically
  ) &
  theme(
```

### De-composed covariates

```{r decomposed covariates, include=FALSE}

# covariate models (decomposed to within and between for policy and support)

long_data <- long_data %>%
  mutate(familiar_num = as.numeric(as.character(familiar)))

# between-person (person/grand mean centred), averages the mean for each persons two scores

long_data <- long_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(support_b = mean(support, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

long_data <- long_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(policy_b = mean(policy, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

long_data <- long_data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(familiar_b = mean(familiar_num, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# within person, takes away the averaged mean for each individual score

long_data <- long_data %>%
  mutate(support_w = support - support_b)

long_data <- long_data %>%
  mutate(policy_w = policy - policy_b)

long_data <- long_data %>%
  mutate(familiar_w = familiar_num - familiar_b)

# models

dcov_c <- lmer(competence ~ motive*imprint + party + policy_b + policy_w + + familiar_b + familiar_w + support_b + support_w + self_ideology + (1|id),
           data = long_data, REML = FALSE)
```

### Post-hoc power

```{r}

posthoc_power_rlmer <- function(model, term, alpha = 0.05) {
  coefs <- summary(model)$coefficients
  est <- coefs[term, "Estimate"]
  se  <- coefs[term, "Std. Error"]

  z_crit <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)               # critical z-value
  z_obs  <- abs(est / se)                      # observed test statistic

  power <- 1 - pnorm(z_crit - z_obs)           # one-tailed, multiply by 2 for symmetry
  power
}

# Example:
posthoc_power_rlmer(cov_i_r, "motive1:imprint1")

library(simr)
powerSim(cov_b, test = fixed("motive1:imprint1", method = "z"))

```


### Cohen's D

```{r}

# Step 1: Get fixed effect estimates
fe_competence <- fixef(cov_c_r)

# Step 2: Get standard errors from model summary
se_competence <- summary(cov_c_r)$coefficients[, "Std. Error"]

# Step 3: Get total SD (residual + random effects)
varcomps <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(cov_c_r))
sd_total <- sqrt(sum(varcomps$vcov))

# Step 4: Define predictors of interest
selected_effects <- c("motive1", "imprint1", "motive1:imprint1")
predictor_labels <- c(
  "Intentionality (1 vs 0)",
  "Disclosure (1 vs 0)",
  "Intentionality * Disclosure"
)

# Step 5: Calculate Cohen's d and 95% CI
d_values <- fe_competence[selected_effects] / sd_total
se_d_values <- se_competence[selected_effects] / sd_total
ci_lower <- d_values - 1.96 * se_d_values
ci_upper <- d_values + 1.96 * se_d_values

# Step 6: Build the data frame
effect_df <- data.frame(
  Predictor = predictor_labels,
  `Cohen's d` = round(d_values, 3),
  `95% CI` = paste0("[", round(ci_lower, 3), ", ", round(ci_upper, 3), "]")
)

# Step 7: Create the table
kable(effect_df, format = "html", caption = "Cohen's d and 95% CI for Fixed Effects") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

```

### SESOI

```{r}

tost_from_mixed_model <- function(model, term, sesoi_d = 0.1, alpha = 0.05) {
  # Extract total SD from all variance components (random + residual)
  vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(model))
  sd_total <- sqrt(sum(vc$vcov, na.rm = TRUE))

  # Coefficients table
  sm <- coef(summary(model))
  if (!term %in% rownames(sm)) stop("Term '", term, "' not found in model coefficients.")

  est <- sm[term, "Estimate"]
  se  <- sm[term, "Std. Error"]

  # Degrees of freedom:
  # - lmerTest models provide 'df' per coefficient.
  # - lme4 (no lmerTest) and robustlmm::rlmer use asymptotic (z); use Inf.
  df <- if ("df" %in% colnames(sm)) sm[term, "df"] else Inf

  # Convert to Cohen's d scale using total SD
  d    <- est / sd_total
  se_d <- se  / sd_total

  # TOST statistics for ±SESOI
  t_lower <- (d - (-sesoi_d)) / se_d  # H0: d <= -SESOI  vs H1: d > -SESOI
  t_upper <- (d -  sesoi_d ) / se_d   # H0: d >=  SESOI  vs H1: d <  SESOI

  # p-values (pt with df=Inf reduces to normal cdf)
  p_lower <- pt(t_lower, df = df, lower.tail = FALSE)
  p_upper <- pt(t_upper, df = df, lower.tail = TRUE)

  # 90% CI for d (two one-sided tests equivalence uses 100*(1-2*alpha)% CI)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = df)  # alpha=0.05 -> 90% CI -> use qt(0.95)
  ci_lower <- d - t_crit * se_d
  ci_upper <- d + t_crit * se_d

  structure(list(
    d = as.numeric(d),
    se_d = as.numeric(se_d),
    df = as.numeric(df),
    t_lower = as.numeric(t_lower),
    t_upper = as.numeric(t_upper),
    ci_90 = c(ci_lower, ci_upper),
    p_lower = as.numeric(p_lower),
    p_upper = as.numeric(p_upper),
    equivalent = (p_lower < alpha & p_upper < alpha),
    sesoi_d = sesoi_d,
    term = term
  ), class = "tost_d_result")
}

print.tost_d_result <- function(x, ...) {
  cat("TOST for Cohen's d (SESOI =", x$sesoi_d, "):\n")
  cat(sprintf("  term             : %s\n", x$term))
  cat(sprintf("  d estimate       : %.3f\n", x$d))
  cat(sprintf("  90%% CI for d     : [%.3f, %.3f]\n", x$ci_90[1], x$ci_90[2]))
  cat(sprintf("  Lower bound test : t(%s) = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
              if (is.infinite(x$df)) "Inf" else sprintf("%.1f", x$df),
              x$t_lower, x$p_lower))
  cat(sprintf("  Upper bound test : t(%s) = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
              if (is.infinite(x$df)) "Inf" else sprintf("%.1f", x$df),
              x$t_upper, x$p_upper))
  cat(sprintf("  Equivalence      : %s\n",
              ifelse(x$equivalent, "EQUIVALENT (within SESOI)", "NOT EQUIVALENT")))
}

# rlmer model
tost_from_mixed_model(model = cov_c_r, term = "imprint1", sesoi_d = 0.1)



# interaction terms

tost_from_mixed_model(model = cov_b_r, term = "motive1:imprint1", sesoi_d = 0.1)

```



```{r}

# create word document table

# ---- 1) Helper to tidy an rlmer model ----
tidy_rlmer <- function(fit, model_name) {
  sm <- summary(fit)
  co <- as.data.frame(sm$coefficients)
  co$term <- rownames(co)
  rownames(co) <- NULL
  
  # robustlmm names: "Estimate", "Std. Error", "t value" (Wald-type)
  # compute Wald (z) p-values and 95% Wald CIs
  co <- co %>%
    transmute(
      model     = model_name,
      term,
      estimate  = Estimate,
      std_error = `Std. Error`,
      z_value   = `t value`,
      p_value   = 2 * pnorm(abs(`t value`), lower.tail = FALSE),
      conf_low  = Estimate - 1.96 * `Std. Error`,
      conf_high = Estimate + 1.96 * `Std. Error`
    ) %>%
    # rounding & pretty p
    mutate(
      across(c(estimate, std_error, conf_low, conf_high), ~ round(.x, 2)),
      p_value_raw = p_value,
      p_value = ifelse(p_value < .001, "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", p_value)),
      z_value = round(z_value, 2)
    ) %>%
    # reorder columns
    dplyr::select(model, term, estimate, std_error, conf_low, conf_high, z_value, p_value)
  
  co
}

# ---- Tidy all models and bind together ----
all_tables <- bind_rows(
  tidy_rlmer(comp_r,  "Competence (base)"),
  tidy_rlmer(cov_c_r, "Competence (covariate-adjusted)"),
  tidy_rlmer(int_r,   "Integrity (base)"),
  tidy_rlmer(cov_i_r, "Integrity (covariate-adjusted)"),
  tidy_rlmer(ben_r,   "Benevolence (base)"),
  tidy_rlmer(cov_b_r, "Benevolence (covariate-adjusted)")
)

# Optional: nicer term labels (edit to your taste)
pretty_terms <- c(
  "(Intercept)" = "(Intercept)",
  "motive"      = "Motive (1 vs 0)",
  "imprint"     = "Imprint (1 vs 0)",
  "party"       = "Party (1 vs 0)",
  "policy"      = "Policy alignment",
  "familiar"    = "Prior knowledge (1 vs 0)",
  "support"     = "Pre-existing support",
  "self_ideology" = "Ideology (L→R)",
  "motive:imprint" = "Motive × Imprint"
)

all_tables <- all_tables %>%
  mutate(term = recode(term, !!!pretty_terms, .default = term))

# ---- 4) Split into a list of per-model tables ----
by_model <- group_split(all_tables, model)
model_names <- unique(all_tables$model)

# ---- 5) Build a Word document with one table per model ----
doc <- read_docx()

for (i in seq_along(by_model)) {
  df <- by_model[[i]] %>%
    dplyr::select(term, estimate, std_error, conf_low, conf_high, z_value, p_value)
  
  ft <- flextable(df)
  ft <- autofit(ft)
  ft <- set_header_labels(
    ft,
    term      = "Term",
    estimate  = "Estimate",
    std_error = "SE",
    conf_low  = "95% CI (low)",
    conf_high = "95% CI (high)",
    z_value   = "z",
    p_value   = "p"
  )
  ft <- align(ft, j = c("estimate","std_error","conf_low","conf_high","z_value","p_value"), align = "right", part = "all")
  
  doc <- doc %>%
    body_add_par(model_names[i], style = "heading 2") %>%
    body_add_flextable(ft) %>%
    body_add_par("")  # spacer
}

print(doc, target = "robust_mixed_models_tables.docx")

```

```{r cooks manual, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}

## Influence at the cluster level
infl_c <- influence(cov_c, group = "id") # iteratively refit the model 980 times to identify the influence of each unit j

cd   <- cooks.distance(infl_c)      # extract Cook's D for each unit j
db   <- dfbetas(infl_c)  # matrix of clusters x individual coefficients (DFBETAS)

## n = number of clusters (participants)
G <- length(cd)

## Manual cutoffs
cut_dfbetas <- 2 / sqrt(G) # if absolute values of DFBETAS exceed the cutoff value 2/√nₓ
cut_cookd   <- 4 / G       # or Cook’s D exceeds 4/nₓ

# cut_dfbetas; cut_cookd

## Flags
flag_cd_idx      <- which(cd > cut_cookd)  # identify how many clusters fall below the cut off
flag_db_any_idx  <- which(apply(abs(db), 1, function(x) any(x > cut_dfbetas, na.rm = TRUE)))   # identify how many points in the matrix fall below the cut off

# Extract Cook's D values for the 53 flagged clusters
flag_cd_values <- cd[flag_cd_idx]
summary(flag_cd_values)
quantile(flag_cd_values, probs = c(.50, .75, .90, .95, .99))

# Extract DFBETAS

max_dfbetas <- apply(abs(db), 1, max, na.rm = TRUE)
cut_dfbetas <- 2 / sqrt(length(max_dfbetas))
below_dfbetas <- max_dfbetas[max_dfbetas > cut_dfbetas]
summary(below_dfbetas)
quantile(below_dfbetas, probs = c(.50, .75, .90, .95, .99))

## Map indices -> actual id labels used inside the model
id_levels <- levels(getME(cov_c, "flist")$id)
flag_cd_ids     <- id_levels[flag_cd_idx]
flag_dfbetas_ids<- id_levels[flag_db_any_idx]

length(flag_cd_ids); length(flag_dfbetas_ids)
flag_cd_ids[1:min(10, length(flag_cd_ids))] # look at the top 10          
flag_dfbetas_ids[1:min(10, length(flag_dfbetas_ids))] 

# are these concerning?

summary(cd)
summary(apply(abs(db), 1, max, na.rm = TRUE))

## (Optional) which coefficients are triggering DFBETAS?
# list cluster indices per coefficient that exceed the cutoff
flag_by_coef <- lapply(seq_len(ncol(db)), function(j) which(abs(db[, j]) > cut_dfbetas))
names(flag_by_coef) <- colnames(db)
flag_by_coef  # inspect per-term flags

## Summary table (one row per id)
summary_infl <- tibble(
  id              = id_levels,
  cooksD          = as.numeric(cd),
  max_abs_dfbetas = apply(abs(db), 1, max, na.rm = TRUE),
  cd_flag         = cooksD > cut_cookd,
  dfbetas_flag    = max_abs_dfbetas > cut_dfbetas
) %>%
  arrange(desc(cooksD))

head(summary_infl, 12)

# visreg

library(visreg)

visreg(cov_c, "policy",  partial=TRUE)
visreg(cov_c, "support", partial=TRUE)
visreg(cov_c, "self_ideology", partial=TRUE)
```

```{r cooks manual, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}

## Influence at the cluster level
infl_i <- influence(cov_i, group = "id")
cd   <- cooks.distance(infl_i)      # length = G clusters
db   <- dfbetas(infl_i)  # G x P matrix (clusters x coefficients) 

# cut_dfbetas; cut_cookd

## Flags
flag_cd_idx      <- which(cd > cut_cookd)
flag_db_any_idx  <- which(apply(abs(db), 1, function(x) any(x > cut_dfbetas, na.rm = TRUE)))

# Extract Cook's D 
flag_cd_values <- cd[flag_cd_idx]
summary(flag_cd_values)
quantile(flag_cd_values, probs = c(.50, .75, .90, .95, .99))

# Extract DFBETAS

max_dfbetas <- apply(abs(db), 1, max, na.rm = TRUE)
cut_dfbetas <- 2 / sqrt(length(max_dfbetas))
below_dfbetas <- max_dfbetas[max_dfbetas > cut_dfbetas]
summary(below_dfbetas)
quantile(below_dfbetas, probs = c(.50, .75, .90, .95, .99))

## Map indices -> actual id labels used inside the model
id_levels <- levels(getME(cov_i, "flist")$id)
flag_cd_ids     <- id_levels[flag_cd_idx]
flag_dfbetas_ids<- id_levels[flag_db_any_idx]

length(flag_cd_ids); length(flag_dfbetas_ids)
flag_cd_ids[1:min(10, length(flag_cd_ids))]           # peek
flag_dfbetas_ids[1:min(10, length(flag_dfbetas_ids))] # peek

## (Optional) which coefficients are triggering DFBETAS?
# list cluster indices per coefficient that exceed the cutoff
flag_by_coef <- lapply(seq_len(ncol(db)), function(j) which(abs(db[, j]) > cut_dfbetas))
names(flag_by_coef) <- colnames(db)
flag_by_coef  # inspect per-term flags

## Summary table (one row per id)
summary_infl <- tibble(
  id              = id_levels,
  cooksD          = as.numeric(cd),
  max_abs_dfbetas = apply(abs(db), 1, max, na.rm = TRUE),
  cd_flag         = cooksD > cut_cookd,
  dfbetas_flag    = max_abs_dfbetas > cut_dfbetas
) %>%
  arrange(desc(cooksD))

head(summary_infl, 12)
```

## Robust model fit 

```{r}

library(robustlmm)

## COMPETENCE

## Robust mixed model (M-estimation)
cov_c_r <- robustlmm::rlmer(
  competence ~ motive*imprint + party + policy + familiar + support + self_ideology +
    (1 | id),
  data = long_data)

summary(cov_c_r)

## Wald-style CIs for fixed effects from the robust vcov:
b  <- fixef(cov_c_r)
SE <- sqrt(diag(vcov(cov_c_r)))
ci <- cbind(lower = b - 1.96*SE, upper = b + 1.96*SE)
round(ci, 3)

## Compare fixed effects from ML vs robust:
cbind(ML = fixef(cov_c), Robust = fixef(cov_c_r))

# Single-parameter Wald tests (z and p)
cf <- summary(cov_c_r)$coefficients   # Estimate, Std. Error, etc.
z  <- cf[, "Estimate"] / cf[, "Std. Error"]
p  <- 2 * pnorm(abs(z), lower.tail = FALSE)

wald_table <- cbind(cf[, c("Estimate","Std. Error")], z = z, `Pr(>|z|)` = p)
round(wald_table, 4)

## INTEGRITY

## Robust mixed model (M-estimation)
cov_i_r <- rlmer(
  integrity ~ motive*imprint + party + policy + familiar + support + self_ideology +
    (1 | id),
  data = long_data)

## decomposed covariates

dcov_i_r <- rlmer(integrity ~ motive*imprint + party + policy_b + policy_w + familiar_b + familiar_w + support_b + support_w + self_ideology + (1|id), data = long_data)

summary(cov_i_r)
summary(dcov_i_r)

# does decomposing help

car::linearHypothesis(
  dcov_i_r,
  c("policy_b = policy_w",
    "familiar_b = familiar_w",
    "support_b = support_w"),
  vcov. = vcov(dcov_i_r),   # robust vcov from rlmer
  test  = "Chisq"
)

## Wald-style CIs for fixed effects from the robust vcov:
b  <- fixef(dcov_i_r)
SE <- sqrt(diag(vcov(dcov_i_r)))
ci <- cbind(lower = b - 1.96*SE, upper = b + 1.96*SE)
round(ci, 3)

## Compare fixed effects from ML vs robust:
cbind(Robust = fixef(cov_i_r), Decomposed = fixef(dcov_i_r))

# Single-parameter Wald tests (z and p)
cf <- summary(dcov_i_r)$coefficients   # Estimate, Std. Error, etc.
z  <- cf[, "Estimate"] / cf[, "Std. Error"]
p  <- 2 * pnorm(abs(z), lower.tail = FALSE)

wald_table <- cbind(cf[, c("Estimate","Std. Error")], z = z, `Pr(>|z|)` = p)
round(wald_table, 4)

```

### Causal mediation

```{r causal mediation, eval=FALSE}

# 0) Build a common analysis dataset (same rows for both models)
med.dat <- long_data %>%
  dplyr::select(id, vote, motive, imprint, party, competence) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na() %>%                 # ensure identical row set
  mutate(
    id      = as.factor(id),           
    vote    = as.numeric(vote)         # 0/1 numeric for glmer
  ) %>%
  mutate(vote = vote - 1)

## 1) Mediator model (random intercept)
med.fit <- nlme::lme(
  fixed   = competence ~ motive + imprint + party,
  random  = ~ 1 | id,
  data    = med.dat,
  na.action = na.omit
)

med.fit <- lmer(
  competence ~ motive + imprint + party + (1 | id),
  data = med.dat
)

# 2) Outcome model as GLM (logit) — no random effect
out.fit <- glm(
  vote ~ motive + competence + imprint + party,
  data   = med.dat,
  family = binomial("logit")
)

## 3) Mediation (ACME/ADE/Total; bootstrap CIs recommended)
med.out <- mediate(
  model.m   = med.fit,
  model.y   = out.fit,
  treat     = "motive",
  mediator  = "competence",
  boot      = FALSE,
  cluster = med.dat$id,
  sims      = 1000
)


# no cluster within med and out models

med.fit <- lm(competence ~ motive + imprint + party, data = med.dat)


```

# mediation with Lavaan 

Is the positive effect of viewing the digital imprint mediated through it looking more professional?

```{r}

aesthetic <- '

     # define the latent variables
     
     l_competence =~ comp + skill + know
     l_integrity =~ princ + truth + sinc
     l_benevolence =~ emp + warm + kind
     
     # set the direct paths
     
     l_competence ~ c1*imprint
     l_integrity ~ c2*imprint
     l_benevolence ~ c3*imprint
     look ~ a*imprint
     l_competence ~ b1*look
     l_integrity ~ b2*look
     l_benevolence ~ b3*look
     
     # outcome covariances
     
     l_competence ~~ l_integrity
     l_integrity ~~ l_benevolence
     l_competence ~~ l_benevolence
     
     # set the indirect paths 
     
     indirect_comp := c1*b1
     indirect_int := c2*b2
     indirect_ben := c3*b2
     
     # total effects
     
     total_comp := c1 + (a*b1)
     total_int := c2 + (a*b2)
     total_ben := c3 + (a*b3)

'

model <- '
  level: 1
    # Within (L1) measurement
    competence_w =~ comp + skill + know
    integrity_w =~ princ + truth + sinc
    benevolence_w =~ emp + warm + kind
    look_w =~ look

    # Within (L1) structural
    look_w ~ a*imprint
    competence_w ~ b1*look_w + cprime*imprint
    integrity_w ~ b2*look_w + cprime*imprint
    benevolence_w ~ b3*look_w + cprime*imprint

    # Defined (within-level) effects
    ind_comp   := a*b1
    ind_int    := a*b2
    ind_ben    := a*b3
    total_comp := cprime + ind_comp
    total_int  := cprime + ind_int
    total_ben  := cprime + ind_ben

  level: 2
    
    competence_b =~ comp + skill + know
    integrity_b =~ princ + truth + sinc
    benevolence_b =~ emp + warm + kind
    look_b =~ look
'

aes_med <- sem(model, data = long_data, estimator = "MLR", cluster = "id", meanstructure=TRUE, fixed.x=TRUE)

summary(aes_med, fit.measures = TRUE)

```

```{r}

model <- '
  ########################
  # Within-person (Level 1)
  ########################
  level: 1

    # Measurement (within)
    competence_w  =~ comp + skill + know
    integrity_w   =~ princ + truth + sinc
    benevolence_w =~ emp + warm + kind

    # Structural (within) — observed look, not a single-indicator latent
    look ~ a*imprint                        # path a (within)
    competence_w  ~ b1*look + c1*imprint    # mediator b1 and direct c1
    integrity_w   ~ b2*look + c2*imprint
    benevolence_w ~ b3*look + c3*imprint

    # Allow residual correlations among the three latent outcomes (within)
    competence_w  ~~ integrity_w + benevolence_w
    integrity_w   ~~ benevolence_w

    # Indirect and total effects (within)
    ind_comp   := a*b1
    ind_int    := a*b2
    ind_ben    := a*b3
    total_comp := c1 + ind_comp
    total_int  := c2 + ind_int
    total_ben  := c3 + ind_ben

  #######################
  # Between-person (Level 2)
  #######################
  level: 2

    # Measurement (between)
    competence_b  =~ comp + skill + know
    integrity_b   =~ princ + truth + sinc
    benevolence_b =~ emp + warm + kind

    # Between-level correlations (optional but recommended)
    competence_b  ~~ integrity_b + benevolence_b
    integrity_b   ~~ benevolence_b
'

fit <- sem(
  model, data = long_data,
  cluster   = "id",     # <-- your person ID
  estimator = "MLR",    # robust SEs/tests
  missing   = "fiml",
  std.lv    = TRUE
)

summary(fit, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE, ci = TRUE)
parameterEstimates(fit, standardized = TRUE, ci = TRUE)

```
